conceptual.anchor: AuthorityChain: Authoritative Source → Authority → Decision → Rule → Derived Rule → Implementation → Verification. Generic 'KnowledgeAuthority' or 'AuthorityReference,' not 'GitaAuthority.'

pairs_touching.what_says_this: Group evidence G0288 explicitly states the Chapter 4 exercise (B, Step 156a) is 'in the same series as the B0020 gita-chapter3-validation-exercise' (A), applying the identical stress-test methodology to the next Gita chapter and producing new H-nn invariants; STRING-SIMILARITY (Jaccard 0.60) corroborates the shared format.
pairs_touching.what_would_make_this_wrong: A quote showing the Chapter 4 exercise used a materially different methodology from Chapter 3's, breaking series continuity.

rationale_evidence.anchor: Knowledge ≠ Document. Knowledge = Content + Lineage + Authority + Transmission + Context.
rationale_evidence.statement: Derives from the chapter's description of a broken succession (Kṛṣṇa->Vivasvān->Manu->Ikṣvāku) that knowledge is not reducible to a document but a composite of content, lineage, authority, transmission, and context.

States Chapter 4's emphasis on authorized succession (and warning against independently manufactured process) validates the existing Governance Runtime chain (Proposal->Decision->Implementation->Verification / Governance->Declared Rule->Implementation->Assurance).

rationale_evidence.anchor: DETERMINISTIC, EMPIRICAL, DERIVED, INTERPRETIVE, GOVERNANCE, UNKNOWN. R(x)∈{true,false} vs P(H|E).
rationale_evidence.statement: Argues KnowledgeOS should not reduce every governance decision to Bayesian probability — some rules are deterministic, others uncertain, others qualitative judgments — and proposes a six-value epistemic-type taxonomy for the kernel.

rationale_evidence.anchor: MultipleProcesses → CommonHigherPurpose. Static Analysis, Runtime Testing, Human Review, AI Analysis, Evidence Collection, Governance Review → ArchitectureAssurance. But Evidence_1+Evidence_2+Evidence_3 ≠ Truth; each Evidence_i → specific claim.
rationale_evidence.statement: Uses the chapter's account of multiple forms of yajña (sacrifice/practice) converging on a common purpose to validate the Step-154 Assurance Orchestrator (multiple evidence-producing mechanisms converging on one verification objective), while warning against collapsing multiple evidence items into an undifferentiated 'truth' — each item retains its own scope/reliability/provenance/temporal validity/method, avoiding pseudo-precision.

rationale_evidence.anchor: Knowledge, Authority, Context, Inquiry, Decision, Action, Evidence, Verification, Governance — should not all be one 'Knowledge' aggregate.
rationale_evidence.statement: Gives a DDD verdict reinforcing at least nine conceptual boundaries and warns against collapsing them into a single aggregate as an architectural failure; adds 'Knowledge Lineage/Provenance' as a cross-cutting first-class concern to the bounded-context sketch Knowledge->Context->Action->Evidence->Assurance->Governance.

rationale_evidence.anchor: Agent recommended X, system succeeded — does not prove Recommendation(X)→Success(X) causally. Observation ≠ Explanation.
rationale_evidence.statement: States a correlation-vs-causation warning specific to AI agent recommendations, requiring preservation of action/intervention/observed result/confounders/evidence, and restates a four-way non-collapse chain: Observation≠Interpretation, Interpretation≠Decision, Decision≠Execution, Execution≠Verification — called one of the strongest architectural properties built so far.

rationale_evidence.anchor: Ch1 Observation. Ch2 Knowledge (distinguish known from apparent). Ch3 Knowledge→Action. Ch4 Knowledge→Lineage→Context→Action→Evidence→Verification.
rationale_evidence.statement: Synthesizes a four-chapter progression across the ongoing Gita-lens validation series (Chapters 1-4), arguing the progression is 'remarkably close to the KnowledgeOS architecture we have independently constructed.'

Derives from the chapter's description of a broken succession (Kṛṣṇa->Vivasvān->Manu->Ikṣvāku) that knowledge is not reducible to a document but a composite of content, lineage, authority, transmission, and context. [S1050]

States Chapter 4's emphasis on authorized succession (and warning against independently manufactured process) validates the existing Governance Runtime chain (Proposal->Decision->Implementation->Verification / Governance->Declared Rule->Implementation->Assurance). [S1050]

Argues KnowledgeOS should not reduce every governance decision to Bayesian probability — some rules are deterministic, others uncertain, others qualitative judgments — and proposes a six-value epistemic-type taxonomy for the kernel. [S1050]

Uses the chapter's account of multiple forms of yajña (sacrifice/practice) converging on a common purpose to validate the Step-154 Assurance Orchestrator (multiple evidence-producing mechanisms converging on one verification objective), while warning against collapsing multiple evidence items into an undifferentiated 'truth' — each item retains its own scope/reliability/provenance/temporal validity/method, avoiding pseudo-precision. [S1050]

Gives a DDD verdict reinforcing at least nine conceptual boundaries and warns against collapsing them into a single aggregate as an architectural failure; adds 'Knowledge Lineage/Provenance' as a cross-cutting first-class concern to the bounded-context sketch Knowledge->Context->Action->Evidence->Assurance->Governance. [S1050]

States a correlation-vs-causation warning specific to AI agent recommendations, requiring preservation of action/intervention/observed result/confounders/evidence, and restates a four-way non-collapse chain: Observation≠Interpretation, Interpretation≠Decision, Decision≠Execution, Execution≠Verification — called one of the strongest architectural properties built so far. [S1050]

Synthesizes a four-chapter progression across the ongoing Gita-lens validation series (Chapters 1-4), arguing the progression is 'remarkably close to the KnowledgeOS architecture we have independently constructed.' [S1050]
